newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cobalt prices may rise up to $30 by July - traders.
newsitem.headline: Cobalt prices may rise up to $30 by July - traders.

text.p: The price of cobalt could increase up to US$30 per pound within the next two or three months, a senior cobalt industry source said on Wednesday, echoing the views of others at a conference.
"The cobalt price, between now and the next two or three months could hit $30 per pound again," said Ed Kielty, head of U.S.-based Hall Chemical Company.
He said that the U.S. Defense Logistics Agency stockpile would continue to be an overhang factor, and that Zaire would continue to overshadow perceptions.
He was addressing industry representatives at a conference in Hong Kong organised by the Cobalt Development Institute.
"The market is an exercise in leverage, the question is who has it," Kielty said.

"You've got the DLA currently after the market, you've got Zaire, even though it will be sorted out at some stage.. you've also had the Zambians with slightly lower production rates at the moment, so those are the three negatives on supply side," said another cobalt trader.
"You've got very robust demand at the moment, there is a strong possiblity that the price moves up another two to three dollars," he said.

He said that Russian shipments from the port of Dudinka would likely be delayed due to seasonal flooding from the middle of May to the end of July, which effectively meant no Russian shipments coming into the market.
"I've already done business at this conference for $22.90 for cobalt ingots," one trader said.
With strong demand, consumers had little choice but to buy at current firm prices, another source said.
"U.S. consumers had been lulled into a sense of false security and did not buy forward," said another senior cobalt source.
"They were told 'don't worry, don't worry,' so instead of buying at $17-18 forward, now for new material, with the DLA taken away from calculations, they have to pay higher prices," he said.
Not buying was as risky as buying, he said.
According to a cobalt expert, the market would probably be close to balanced, and when the market was close to balanced, it could be manipulated.
"Either you say cobalt was overvalued at $30 two years ago, or it's undervalued at $25," one trader said.
There were a few dissenting voices which said simply that supplies were adequate.
"We're now at about $23/24, I could see it being there for a while," one industry source said.
